function: Blind digital over-the-air gradient aggregation: closed-form q-QAM encoder/decoder and receive beamforming from summed channels, no device CSI; no learned physical-layer component (p. 5-6).
system: ES with Nr antennas (10 to 800 tested) and K=20 single-antenna devices, OFDM over a fading MAC, no RIS, carrier frequency not stated (p. 4, 9-10).
method: Non-learned closed-form scheme (q-QAM SumComp coding, sum-channel beamformer); the learned element is a CNN trained by federated SGD with Adam on MNIST and CIFAR-10 (p. 5-6, 9).
data_channel: Simulated i.i.d. Gaussian fading CN(0, sigma_h^2 I) plus AWGN, no path loss or standard model; MNIST and CIFAR-10 for the FL task (p. 4, 9).
test_conditions: Sweeps over antennas Nr (10-800), QAM order (64, 256), noise and fading variance, and homogeneous versus heterogeneous data; no train/test channel mismatch (p. 9-10).
baselines: Error-free baseline and the analog blind FEEL scheme of [17] on test accuracy; OFDMA and the analog scheme on communication latency (p. 9-11).
metrics: Test accuracy versus communication rounds (MNIST, CIFAR-10), MSE of the gradient and of the summation versus antennas, quantization error, and communication latency (p. 8-11).
complexity: none; only a qualitative remark that complexity is almost identical to the analog scheme, referring to [26] (p. 6).
openness: none; MNIST and CIFAR-10 are public datasets of the learning task alone, and no code or data link is given (p. 9).
q1_support: p. 9: "The channel coefficients and noise for all sub-channels are generated according to" complex Gaussian draws CN(0, sigma_h^2 I); a custom simulator with no path loss, 3GPP, or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 10: "Figure 5(a) shows the test accuracy over the communication rounds for various numbers of antennas at the ES" is a parameter sweep with each setting trained anew; the paper never trains in one condition and tests in another.
q3_support: p. 9: "compared to the baseline (error-free) and blind FEEL scheme proposed in [17]" (earlier published analog aggregation design, test accuracy, Fig. 6); p. 11: "in comparison to analog and orthogonal communication methods" (OFDMA, latency, Fig. 7).
q4_support: p. 6: "the computational complexity of ChannelCompFed is almost identical to the analog scheme" is only qualitative and defers to [26]; no order, FLOPs, or runtime is reported, and the latency study (p. 11) counts time slots.
q5_support: p. 9: "The machine learning task is image classification for the MNIST [36] dataset and CIFAR-10 [37]" are public datasets of the learning task alone; the channels are simulated and the paper gives no code or data link.
notes: Included as area 7: digital over-the-air computation for federated edge learning (p. 2). The physical layer is closed-form (p. 5-6), so it passes the learning check only through the rule for federated learning over the air (learned element is the CNN trained across devices); the reviewer should confirm. q3 is borderline: earlier design [17] (accuracy, p. 9) with the error-free reference and OFDMA (latency, p. 11) as the non-learned comparators.
